paper_title: COSMI: COmpositional Synthesis of Multi-object Interactions

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Generative models of human-object interaction are bounded by the data that exists: everyday activities involve several objects, but most captured datasets record one at a time, as multi-object capture is combinatorially expensive. Our observation is that interactions are local, so single-object captures already contain the parts of multi-object activities. We compose them: contact-consistent clips of single interactions, mirrored to balance the hands, transfer between bodies, and a language model and geometric checks admit only the pairings that are plausible, semantically and physically. Therefore, the dataset grows combinatorially with the clips rather than recording time. The COSMI dataset holds 222k sequences and 275 hours with up to five objects, nearly thirty times the largest multi-object capture, and can be extended by adding datasets or even hand-object recordings. On this data we train the COSMI method, a text-to-interaction diffusion transformer that follows how the data is built: weight-shared object slots generate a variable number of objects, predicted relative to the body parts that move them. On a benchmark with an unseen object and unseen interaction combinations, models trained on the dataset generalize to the unseen combinations. COSMI outperforms baselines in text alignment and contact accuracy, where its margin is largest on the unseen object. Code, models, and the dataset pipeline will be released on the project page: https://ptrvilya.github.io/cosmi.

sections.title: INTRODUCTION
sections.content: Generating 3D human-object interaction (HOI) serves animation, embodied AI, and augmented reality, from humanoid controllers and robot policies that learn from HOI motion (Xu et al., 2025b; Wang et al., 2025b) to egocentric assistants (Banerjee et al., 2025; Ma et al., 2024; Petrov et al., 2026) and composite animation such as sitting down while carrying an object (Pan et al., 2025). The activities these applications target are frequently multi-object: in the KIT whole-body database, 99 of the 262 object-related motions involve two or more objects (Mandery et al., 2016). Like other generative models, motion generators improve with data (Wang et al., 2025a; Xu et al., 2025a), so what HOI generators can produce is bounded by the interaction data that exists. On the data side, HOI datasets mostly record one person with one object (Taheri et al., 2020), and the generators trained on them inherit this scope (Xu et al., 2023; Diller & Dai, 2024; Peng et al., 2025). Capturing several objects at once is expensive, and the cost grows combinatorially with the objects, body parts, and pairings (Xie et al., 2024), so captured multi-object datasets stay below ten hours (Lv et al., 2024; Kim et al., 2025; Lu et al., 2025), against 21.8 in the single-object collection InterAct (Xu et al., 2025a). On the model side, generators are built for one object (Diller & Dai, 2024; Pi et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2023), and the few multi-object ones train one model per object count (Lv et al., 2024; He et al., 2025) or pad fixed state (Zhang et al., 2024a) and leave implicit which body part moves which object. The concurrent SK-HOI (Peng et al., 2026) handles variable number of objects in three separate stages. There is no multi-object data at single-object scale, and no end-to-end generator for variable number of objects grounded to the body parts that move them. Synthetic and composed data has closed comparable gaps before (Black et al., 2023; Xie et al., 2024; Mandlekar et al., 2023), and closest to our setting, SINC composes simultaneous actions by taking each body part from the clip whose action uses it (Athanasiou et al., 2023). Our observation is that interactions with objects are local in the same way: cup is held by hand, chair supports the pelvis, ball is kicked by foot, and the rest of the body is free. The limb that performs one interaction can therefore be transferred, together with its object, to body that performs another, and multi-object interactions can be composed from single-object captures  (Fig. 1)  , which exist at scale. The composition is only as good as its gating: from contact-consistent clips of single interactions, language model decides which can plausibly happen at once, and geometric checks keep only the compositions that stay in contact and free of penetration  (Fig. 2)  . Mirroring the one-handed and one-footed clips balances the left and right hands, which captured interactions skew to the right. The resulting COSMI dataset contains 222k sequences and 275 hours of motion, nearly thirty times the largest captured multi-object dataset (Lv et al., 2024). Its physical plausibility stays close to the parent captures (Section A.1), and since nothing in the composition is specific to dataset, it grows by adding rule rather than recording session, even from hand-object recordings (Section 5). Such data calls for generator for variable number of objects. COSMI is single diffusion transformer that denoises the person and set of objects from prompt and initial poses. Its object slots share their weights, so no parameter depends on the object count, and one model generates one to five objects. Each object is predicted relative to the joint that drives it, which part-assignment head reads from these conditions, and text tokens link the words of the prompt to the objects. On benchmark that holds out an unseen object and five unseen combinations, such as walking-with-anapple (while walking-only and apple-eating stay in training), COSMI and the baselines trained on the COSMI dataset alike generalize to the unseen combinations. COSMI outperforms HIMO (Lv et al., 2024) and multi-object adaptations of MDM and PriorMDM (Tevet et al., 2023; Shafir et al., 2024) in text alignment and contact accuracy, where its margin is largest on the unseen object. In summary, our contributions are: Composition of multi-object interactions from single-object captures, and the COSMI dataset: 222k sequences with up to five objects, left and right balanced by mirroring, extensible by design. The COSMI method: text-conditioned diffusion transformer for variable number of objects, with joint-relative prediction, part assignment, auxiliary losses, and contact-consistent guidance. benchmark on the COSMI dataset that tests generalization to an unseen object and to unseen interaction combinations. Code, models, and the dataset pipeline will be released.

sections.title: 2 RELATED WORK
sections.content: Human-object interaction datasets. Most full-body interaction datasets, captured with markerbased motion capture or multi-view video, record one person with one object (Taheri et al., 2020; Bhatnagar et al., 2022; Huang et al., 2024; Li et al., 2023; Zhang et al., 2023b; Zhao et al., 2024), later also with articulated objects (Jiang et al., 2023; Fan et al., 2023). Full-body datasets with several objects per sequence are recent and small  (Table 1)  : HIMO records two or three small rigid objects (Lv et al., 2024), ParaHome and HUMOTO articulated household objects (Kim et al., 2025; Lu et al., 2025), and HOI-M3, CORE4D, and MMHOI several people (Zhang et al., 2024a; Liu et al., 2025; Kogashi et al., 2026). Hand-object datasets omit the body but record more hours and objects, often several at once (Hampali et al., 2020; Chao et al., 2021; Zhan et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2024; Banerjee et al., 2025; Fu et al., 2025), and body fitted to such recording turns it into source clip for our pipeline (Section 5). Interaction data has also been generated procedurally, placed into scenes, augmented, or recovered from video (Xie et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2022; Xu et al., 2025a; Zhang et al., 2026; Xie et al., 2026), always with one object. The COSMI dataset instead composes these single-object captures into multi-object sequences: every source clip pairs with every compatible target and composed sequences serve as targets again, so the number of sequences grows combinatorially with the clips rather than linearly with recording time  (Table 1)  . Compositionality in motion and interaction modeling. Animation has long composed captured clips without objects, in time with motion graphs (Kovar et al., 2002) and across body parts by splicing (Ikemoto & Forsyth, 2004; Heck et al., 2006). SINC revisits spatial composition with language, composing the body parts of two clips into training data from GPT-3 part labels, and leaves the semantic compatibility to future work (Athanasiou et al., 2023). Later models annotate, coordinate, or blend parts (Li et al., 2026; Zou et al., 2024; Jiang et al., 2025) or compose actions in time at inference (Athanasiou et al., 2022; Shafir et al., 2024; Petrovich et al., 2024; Barquero et al., 2024). Language models also plan compositions at inference, as contact chains, joint-contact pairs, affordance graphs, or plans (Xiao et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2024b; Li & Dai, 2026; Xu et al., 2024; Sun et al., 2026), while we use one offline to infer the semantic plausibility of clip combinations (Section 3). Composed training data exists for multi-person motion, by random placement (Shan et al., 2024) or with LLM guidance and learned filter (Wu et al., 2026), and for interactions only as static poses (Zhao et al., 2022) or as segments and models composed at inference (Lv et al., 2024; Na et al., 2025). We extend body-part composition to interactions with objects, at the data level and across datasets, with object transfer across bodies, semantic gating, and physical checks. Text-driven interaction synthesis. Text-to-motion generation rests on diffusion and token models trained on HumanML3D (Guo et al., 2022; Tevet et al., 2023; Zhang et al., 2024b; Chen et al., 2023; Zhang et al., 2023a; Guo et al., 2024) and, recently, on million-clip corpora (Wang et al., 2025a), two orders of magnitude larger than any captured interaction dataset. Interaction generators extend them to body and one object (Ghosh et al., 2023; Xu et al., 2023; Li et al., 2023; 2024; Peng et al., 2025; Diller & Dai, 2024; Xu et al., 2024; Petrov et al., 2025; Ron et al., 2026; Ji et al., 2026; Pan et al., 2026; Jung et al., 2026; Cai et al., 2026), including articulated ones (Pi et al., 2025), and grasp synthesis models the fingers in contact (Taheri et al., 2022; Wu et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2021; Cha et al., 2024; Christen et al., 2024; Zhang et al., 2025). Generators for several objects are few: HIMO trains separate models for two and three objects (Lv et al., 2024), SyncDiff one model per object configuration, conditioned on label phrases (He et al., 2025), and Dex2HOI one stream per object for at most two, both in the hands (Pratikaki et al., 2026). HOI-M3 pads preset state and takes no text (Zhang et al., 2024a), and HOI-PAGE optimizes each sequence zero-shot for minutes (Li & Dai, 2026). The concurrent SK-HOI covers variable number of objects with zero-padded slots, but generates in three separately trained stages followed by minutes of test-time optimization per sequence (Peng et al., 2026). COSMI instead is one text-conditioned diffusion transformer with no parameter tied to the object count, which generates one to five objects, articulated and worn, in single stage and grounds the objects to the body parts that move them.

We therefore extract contact-consistent clips from the source sequences, annotate them with semantic information from language model, and mirror them to balance the left and right hands. To combine the clips, we rely on this semantic information to pair plausible matches, followed by geometric checks of the physical plausibility of the result  (Fig. 2)  . We build on GRAB (Taheri et al., 2020), BEHAVE (Bhatnagar et al., 2022), InterCap (Huang et al., 2024), OMOMO (Li et al., 2023), and ARCTIC (Fan et al., 2023), with BEHAVE and InterCap in their InterAct (Xu et al., 2025a) versions, and on CMU walking sequences from AMASS (Mahmood et al., 2019) selected with BABEL labels (Punnakkal et al., 2021). All sources are unified to genderneutral SMPL-X (Pavlakos et al., 2019) body at 30 fps in common frame, and every object is template mesh with rigid transform per frame, one per part for articulated objects (Section C.1). Contact-based extraction. We build the dataset from atomic clips, segments in which person performs single interaction and stays in contact with the object from the first frame to the last, so that the acting limb and the object can be lifted out with their contact intact. Thirteen interaction rules specify the interaction types by the body parts that must and must not touch the object, by pose constraints such as an upright torso, and by the local reference joints relative to which the object is expressed (Section C.2). We evaluate every rule per frame, with contact defined as proximity below 5 cm to the object surface, and take contiguous windows of at least 3 as atomic clips, 1,491 in total. Holds and worn objects reduce to single representative frame, and the walking rule admits whole sequences. In composition, source rules cover the manipulation of small objects with one or both hands and passive holds (GRAB, ARCTIC). Target rules cover the interactions that engage the whole body, sitting, moving large objects, foot interactions, and walking (BEHAVE, InterCap, OMOMO, AMASS), and augmentation rules the worn backpack and eyeglasses (BEHAVE, GRAB). Global trajectories do not transfer between bodies, so we express each object relative to the body part performing its interaction, the local reference joints its rule specifies, such as the wrist or the foot. The COSMI dataset contains 221,677 sequences and 275 hours of motion from 59 subjects and 36 objects, seven of them articulated, with up to five objects per sequence and left and right hands balanced at 49/51  (Table 1)  . Every composed sequence inherits the capture quality of its parents, which we verify with the metrics of HUMOTO (Lu et al., 2025) on the composed sequences and on their parent recordings (Section A.1). Foot sliding is unchanged, since composition alters neither the lower body nor the global trajectory, and jerk and penetration change by less than the captured datasets differ among themselves, human jerk the most, by up to half. Extensibility and benchmark. Nothing in the composition is specific to source dataset: the rules are stated by contacts, pose constraints, and reference joints on the unified body, so any clip on this body enters through rule, as the AMASS walking sequences do. Partial observations enter as well, since every interaction is stored relative to the body part that performs it. hand-object recording becomes source clip once body is fitted to it, which is less obvious, so we demonstrate it with HOT3D (Section 5). The exhaustive enumeration also makes generalization testable: pairing such as walking with an apple can be held out as whole while walking and eating an apple remain in training. Our benchmark builds on this and tests how well model generalizes to five such unseen combinations and to an unseen object, held out with all its sequences (Section 5).

The text prompt is encoded with CLIP (Radford et al., 2021) and enters the model both as pooled sentence embedding and as the sequence of word-piece embeddings, the text tokens W. Following HIMO (Lv et al., 2024), we also condition on the first frame of the window, the initial pose of the person and of every object. Each object is further described by its name and by an embedding of its geometry, computed from basis point set features (Prokudin et al., 2019) with hierarchical encoder (Section D.3). Since the object names appear in the captions and are encoded with the same CLIP model, the text tokens, as in MotionDiffuse (Zhang et al., 2024b), let every object be related to the words that refer to it, which the pooled embedding cannot. Object slots. The token streams of the objects, which we call slots, receive no slot-specific embedding: all slots share the input and output projections and differ only in their conditioning, and masks exclude empty slots from attention and from the per-object losses. The network is therefore permutation-equivariant with respect to the objects, and none of its parameters depends on their number, which is set at run time rather than in the architecture, with up to five slots in training. Part assignment. We say that joint Jrel drives an object if the object moves with this joint: an object held in hand, worn on the head or back, or kicked with foot is driven by the wrist, head, spine, or foot. chair, in contrast, is not driven but only supports the person who sits on it. lightweight transformer head predicts the driving joints of every object from the conditions alone, supervised with labels derived from contacts and joint motion (Section D.5). Its prediction enters the denoiser as an additional input and selects the decoding: driven object is placed through the relative pose Oj of its driving joint, and an undriven object keeps its absolute pose O. Objective. We use the DDPM formulation (Ho et al., 2020) with cosine noise schedule of 1000 steps (Nichol & Dhariwal, 2021), and the network predicts the clean sample (Ramesh et al., 2022). Training and inference. Windows are cut at random offsets and paired with one of their captions. We drop the text prompt for classifier-free guidance (Ho & Salimans, 2022) and, for robustness to missing inputs, also worn objects, names, and the part-assignment input (Section D.7). Contact-consistent guidance. The model predicts finger-object contacts in ct and foot-floor contacts in ct H, but its geometry does not always agree with them. Since the contact labels decrease with the distance between finger and the object surface and with the speed of foot, predicted contact implies an upper bound on this distance or speed, which holds exactly on the training data. In the last sampling steps, gradient steps on the predicted clean sample penalize violations of these bounds (Eq. (10)), which closes the gaps between fingers and objects and stops planted feet.

sections.title: 5 EXPERIMENTS
sections.content: We evaluate on our benchmark, compare with HIMO on its dataset, and ablate COSMI. Figure 4 shows HOT3D (Banerjee et al., 2025) recordings turned into source clips by fitting body to the headset and the MANO (Romero et al., 2017) hands (Section A.7), and Fig. 5 compares COSMI with the baselines. Composed sequences also animate clothed scans (Wang et al., 2024a) registered as SMPL-X+D (Kostyrko et al., 2026), with held objects re-attached to the hands of the scan (Figs. 1 and 9), and would drive any SMPL-X-anchored avatar (Eskandar et al., 2026) the same way. Data split. split by subject, the common choice for captured datasets, says little about generalization here, because the clips of held-out subject would still occur in thousands of training sequences. Instead, we split by composition and hold out what multi-object model is expected to generalize to. Baselines. The closest prior work is HIMO (Lv et al., 2024), whose benchmark also adapts MDM (Tevet et al., 2023) and PriorMDM (Shafir et al., 2024) to several objects. We re-implement MDM and PriorMDM on our representation with our initial-pose conditioning, schedule, and losses, but with pooled text embedding and small geometry encoder, so that each is single model evaluated in all tiers. MDM has one token per frame, whereas PriorMDM has separate human and object streams with one communication block. HIMO supports rigid objects only, so its two models are trained on the twoand three-object tiers in its format and scored with our evaluator. The concurrent SK-HOI (Peng et al., 2026) is not compared, since its full code is unavailable and its test-time optimization of about four minutes per sequence is out of reach for 35k sequences. Implementation details. COSMI has 30.4M parameters, between MDM (20.7M) and PriorMDM (39.6M), and trains in eight hours on one RTX 5090. window is generated in 0.16 with classifierfree guidance, and in 1.1 with the contact-consistent guidance (Section D.8). Comparison with baselines. Table 2 and Fig. 5 compare the methods in the all-objects tier, COSMI with the contact-consistent guidance of Section 4. COSMI obtains the best FID, Rprecision, MM-Dist, and foot sliding, and its penetration stays at the ground-truth level, the residual penetration of the captures, which the baselines exceed. COSMI has the lowest hinge-angle error but the smallest hinge sweep, two thirds of the ground truth (Section A.6). The twoand three-object tiers agree  (Table 3)  , the baselines up to seventeen points above the ground-truth penetration with two objects, except that HIMO, trained per tier, has the best top-3 R-precision with three objects. Comparison on the HIMO dataset. To compare with HIMO on captured data, we also re-train COSMI on the HIMO dataset and evaluate it with the evaluator of HIMO (Section A.3). COSMI has the highest top-3 R-precision in both tiers and, with three objects, also the best FID. Ablations. We ablate the guidance, the auxiliary losses, the part assignment, the text tokens and object names, the geometry encoder, and the chunk size, with results in Section A.2. The auxiliary losses matter most, and the part assignment improves both text alignment and contact accuracy. Text tokens and object names improve text alignment, and the guidance significantly decreases foot sliding and hand-object gaps without damaging the other metrics. Generalization. Table 4 reports the contact accuracy on the unseen object and on each unseen combination. On the combinations, all methods match or exceed their accuracy on the whole test set, with one drop of three points, so they appear to learn the base motion and the hand interaction independently of each other. COSMI is the most accurate on every subset, and the unseen object is harder: the baselines lose four to eight points of temporal contact accuracy on the black chair, whereas COSMI stays within one point of its value on the whole test set.

sections.title: 6 CONCLUSIONS
sections.content: Everyday activities combine objects in countless ways, from drinking while sitting to eating an apple while walking, and the combinations to capture grow faster than any recording effort. The COSMI interactions are local, so contact-consistent dataset shows that they need not all be recorded: clip of one interaction carries its limb and object onto body that performs another. language model and geometric checks admit only the combinations that person would plausibly perform and that remain physically valid, so what emerges is not stitched clips but semantically meaningful, realistic multi-object interactions. The result is 222k sequences and 275 hours with up to five objects, balanced between the hands by mirroring and nearly as plausible as their captures. Nothing in the composition is tied to source dataset, so every further capture multiplies the combinations, fullbody datasets through rule and hand-object recordings once body is fitted to them, as HOT3D shows. The COSMI method, text-driven diffusion transformer grounding the objects to the body parts that move them, generates variable number of objects end to end. The baselines and COSMI alike generalize to combinations never seen in training, and COSMI also to an unseen object. Limitations and future work. The composition covers sustained single interactions at once or in sequence. Extending it to multi-stage activities such as cooking or assembling, whose steps and objects depend on each other, and bringing the data together with interactable scenes, where cup is taken from shelf on the way, are the directions we consider most promising. On the method side, the guidance closes the gaps between fingers and objects, but the finger motion has yet to reach the precision of dedicated grasp synthesis. Finally, text is coarse interface: the prompt fixes the objects and actions, but not the path of the person or the timing of sequential actions.

sections.content: Abstract. This appendix extends the experiments of the main paper and completes the description of the dataset and the method. In Section A, we measure the quality of the composed sequences against their parent recordings, ablate the components of the COSMI method, compare with HIMO on its own dataset, and present qualitative results and failure cases. We also show that hand-object recordings enter the composition once body is fitted to them, and we render composed sequences on clothed scans. In Section B, we define the evaluator behind the learned metrics and the physical metrics with their thresholds and units. In Section C, we detail the construction of the dataset, from the preprocessing of the sources and the interaction rules to the mirroring that balances the hands and the feasibility checks of the composition. Finally, in Section D, we describe the COSMI method in full, including the representations of the person and the objects, the architecture, the training objective, and the contact-consistent guidance. sections.title: A ADDITIONAL RESULTS
sections.content: A.1 QUALITY OF COMPOSED SEQUENCES Table 5 compares, for each of the six sources, the parent recordings with the composed sequences built from them, with the metrics of HUMOTO (Lu et al., 2025): foot sliding and jerk of the human, jerk of the objects, and the depth to which objects penetrate the body and the hands. Foot sliding is unchanged, since composition alters neither the lower body nor the global trajectory. Human jerk rises by fifth to nearly half on GRAB, ARCTIC, InterCap, and AMASS, most in absolute terms for the walking sequences of AMASS, which carry the arm motion of manipulation after composition, and object jerk and penetration change in both directions and worsen by less than the captured datasets differ among themselves, the largest relative rise being the body penetration of InterCap, from 0.17 to 0.40 cm. Objects on walking bodies have no captured counterpart and show the highest object jerk, since they move with the gait. A.2 ABLATIONS Table 6 changes one component of the model at time. Guidance reduces foot sliding by fifth and closes the finger-object gaps: on 512 test windows, the share of predicted contacts that violate their bound (Eq. (9)) by more than 5 mm drops from 18.9 % to 0.9 %. Text alignment and contact accuracy stay unchanged, since the guidance enforces the predicted contacts rather than correcting them, at the cost of slightly more object jerk and penetration. The other variants are sampled without guidance and compare with the unguided model. The auxiliary losses matter most: without them, foot sliding doubles and temporal contact accuracy drops by 17 points. The part assignment improves both text alignment and contacts, whereas the text tokens and the object names improve the text alignment only, by two and one points of top-1 R-precision. Replacing the hierarchical geometry encoder by an MLP changes little, slightly worse top-3 R-precision and multimodal distance against better FID and object jerk, and the chunk size of four balances single-frame object tokens, which lower the temporal contact accuracy by two points, against chunks of eight, which lower the top-1 R-precision by two points. A.3 COMPARISON ON THE HIMO DATASET Table 7 compares COSMI, trained on the HIMO dataset and sampled without guidance, the setting closest to that of HIMO, with the values that HIMO reports for MDM, PriorMDM, and HIMO under its evaluator. COSMI has the highest top-3 R-precision in both tiers, 0.730 and 0.582 against 0.637 and 0.535 for HIMO, and with three objects also the lowest FID and MM-Dist and the diversity closest to the data. With two objects, HIMO, trained for this number of objects alone, has lower FID, 1.481 against 4.896, and lower MM-Dist, and our multimodality is the lowest in both tiers. A.7 HAND-OBJECT RECORDINGS HOT3D (Banerjee et al., 2025) provides the trajectory of the head-mounted device, MANO (Romero et al., 2017) hand poses, and object poses. For every object, we keep the segments in which the head is stable and exactly one object is lifted and in contact with hand, and place neutral SMPL-X template with its head at the tracked head position, facing the object. The rotations of the upper body are then optimized so that the SMPL-X hand vertices match the MANO hands and the head faces the object, with pose prior and temporal smoothness term, and the finger poses are copied from MANO. The resulting clips contain full body with the recorded hands and object, and the interaction rules process them like any other source clip, so HOT3D objects can be composed onto the walking, sitting, and large-object targets of the dataset  (Fig. 8)  . A.8 CLOTHED SCANS We use the SMPL-X+D registrations from (Kostyrko et al., 2026) of the 4D-DRESS scans (Wang et al., 2024a), per-vertex displacements on top of the body model, which we animate through the SMPL-X skinning weights with the joint transforms of the composed sequence. The displacements are attenuated along the forearms and removed on the hands, so that the recorded finger motion is preserved, and the objects are re-attached through their joint-relative transforms, so that held object follows the hand of the scan (Figs. 1 and 9). All figures and videos are rendered with Blendify (Guzov et al., 2024).

sections.title: B METRIC DEFINITIONS
sections.content: B.1 EVALUATOR The learned metrics follow the text-to-motion protocol (Guo et al., 2022) with an evaluator trained on our training split. sequence is described per frame by the 24 joint positions and, per object slot, the 6D rotation, the center of mass, the hinge channel, and presence flag, z-scored with the training statistics. convolutional movement encoder, trained first as an autoencoder on 64frame snippets and downsampling by four, feeds bidirectional GRU motion encoder. The motion encoder is trained together with projection of the frozen CLIP text embedding into common 512dimensional space with contrastive margin loss, margin 3, where pairs with identical canonical captions are never negatives. R-precision and MM-Dist are computed on pools of 32 sequences, FID between the embeddings of the generations and of the ground-truth sequences, and diversity over 100 random pairs, each averaged over the three generations and reported with its 95 % confidence interval. As these metrics depend on the evaluator, we compare them only between methods scored

sections.title: Preprint
sections.content: with the same evaluator. Multimodality (MModal.), reported on the HIMO dataset only, is the mean distance between the embeddings of generations for the same caption, as in HIMO. B.2 PHYSICAL METRICS Foot sliding (Li et al., 2024; Lu et al., 2025) is the horizontal displacement of the ankle and toe joints in frames where they are below height threshold H, 8 cm for the ankles and 4 cm for the toes, which is one on the floor and zero at the threshold, summed, divided by the number of frames, and averaged over the four joints, in mm per frame. Object jerk is the mean norm of the third temporal difference of the object position, as in HUMOTO (Lu et al., 2025), in cm per frame3. Penetration is the fraction of frames in which body vertex lies deeper than 2 cm inside an object, the collision metric of SK-HOI (Peng et al., 2026). Table 5 instead uses the definitions of HUMOTO, whose penetration is the deepest intrusion of the body or hands into the object, averaged over frames. For the contact accuracy (Peng et al., 2026), body marker is in contact when it lies within 2 cm of the object surface: T-Acc is the accuracy of the per-frame contact state, where frame is in contact when any of the 138 markers is, and B-Acc the accuracy of the per-marker states. The hinge-angle error is the mean absolute difference between the generated and the ground-truth hinge angle, wrapped to [π, π], in radians, and the sweep ratio divides the total hinge motion of generated sequence by that of the ground truth. The 95 % confidence intervals of these metrics are below 0.02, and below 0.2 percentage points for penetration.

C.7 MERGE AND FEASIBILITY Figure 13: Composition graph. An arrow leads from every source rule to the rules it can be composed onto. The composed pose is the target pose with the joints of the source action replaced: the wrist, elbow, shoulder, and collar of the acting arm, or both arms for two-handed action. Every manipulation also replaces the two upper spine joints, because the torso bends with reaching arm, whereas passive hold replaces the arm alone. An action that requires gaze adds the neck and head, one that involves the head adds the spine as well, and an object the target already holds moves with its wrist when the spine changes. The source objects and worn objects then follow their reference joints through Eq. (1)  (Fig. 14)  . The composition is kept if every object retains the contacts of its rule in at least half of the frames. It is rejected if, in any frame, an object comes within 1 cm of another object or enters the lower body, the hands enter the lower body, or the arms cross. Walking targets, whose arms swing, tolerate such self-intersections in up to third of the frames. The second action starts 15 frames before the first ends, the spine and head are interpolated between the two over this overlap, and outside its period each source is frozen at its first or last frame together with its object. At decoding, the pose source is selected once per window: the driving joint with the highest average predicted score, wrist scored by the maximum over its fingers. If no joint is predicted as driving or the highest score is below 0.5, the absolute pose is used. The baselines, which have no part-assignment head, select among all six candidate joints by the same contact scores, so an object follows joint only while its predicted contact stays high. D.6 LOSS TERMS The terms Lk of Eq. (5) are ℓ1 errors of the human parameters and of their frame-to-frame differences, of the absolute object pose, of the relative poses in their supervised frames, and of the hinge channel, and cross-stream consistency term. Further terms are squared errors of the object and foot-floor contact scores and foot-skating penalty on the predicted ankles and toes in frames where the ground-truth foot is in contact with the floor. forward-kinematics term compares the joint positions of the predicted rotations with the ground-truth positions, and the binary cross-entropy of the part-assignment head completes the objective. The consistency term poses 100 surface points of the object with each of the seven predicted poses, points on moving part with the predicted hinge angle, and penalizes the ℓ1 distance of the points and of their frame-to-frame differences to the ground truth. All weights λk are 1, except 2 for the human-parameter term. D.7 TRAINING DETAILS We train for 80k steps with batches of 256 windows using Adam (Kingma & Ba, 2015) with learning rate of 5104 and cosine schedule with warm-up, and sample from an exponential moving average of the weights. Training takes eight hours on one RTX 5090. The text prompt is dropped with probability 0.1, replacing the sentence token by learned null embedding and masking the text tokens. Each worn object is included with probability 0.5, an object name by null embedding with probability 0.3, and the part-assignment input is removed with probability 0.1.
